title: Days That Are Kept
subject: world-religions
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten observances from the world's calendars, each with its own season and its own way of being marked.

entries.clue: Full-moon day marking the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing

entries.explanation: Observed by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and some Buddhists, with different reasons given in each tradition.

Forty days of preparation before that feast

factCards.text: The Islamic calendar is purely lunar, so its months move about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year and Ramadan travels through every season.
The Sikh festival of Vaisakhi commemorates the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh at Anandpur in 1699, and coincides with the Punjabi harvest.
Vesak is observed on a full-moon day in April or May; Theravada and Mahayana communities do not always keep it on the same date.
